description: Write the project documentation: a top-level README, the multi-phase ROADMAP, the ARCHITECTURE doc (hybrid LAN + relay transport, E2E crypto, pairing, module layout), and VERIFICATION.md with the on-device + relay-deployment test procedure the user runs. This captures what works in the sandbox vs. what needs the user's Android Studio + a deployed relay, and explicitly documents the 'phone far away still works' remote path.
steps: Create README.md: product name 'Linkup', one-paragraph pitch (Apple-like ecosystem for all-Android devices), the Phase 1 feature list (Universal Clipboard, screenshot/file/photo share), the hybrid transport summary (same Wi-Fi = direct; different networks = relay so it works when the phone is far away), module overview (:core, :relay, :app), and quickstart (sandbox: `./gradlew :core:test :relay:test`; user: open :app in Android Studio, deploy :relay, set relay URL).

Create docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: diagrams-in-text of pairing (QR/short code -> shared secret -> HKDF link key), the Envelope + framing protocol, the LAN path (NSD + direct socket), the relay path (WebSocket, zero-knowledge routing, offline queue), the threat model (relay cannot read payloads; pairing establishes trust), and the Android components (foreground SyncService, clipboard, MediaProjection, SAF).

Create docs/ROADMAP.md: Phase 1 (this work: pairing, E2E, LAN+relay transport, clipboard, screenshot/file share, relay server). Phase 2 ideas (FCM push wake-up for a sleeping remote phone, auto-reconnect polish, multi-file/large-file resumable transfer, notification mirroring). Phase 3 (relay hardening/auth, TLS/own-domain deploy, battery optimization, optional desktop/web client).

Create docs/VERIFICATION.md: (A) sandbox checks already run (`./gradlew :core:test :relay:test`, relay /health). (B) user on-device procedure: build/install on 2+ Android devices, pair via QR, test clipboard + screenshot share on same Wi-Fi, then deploy :relay to a public host (or ngrok/port-forward), set the relay URL in the app, put the phone on mobile data (off the home Wi-Fi) and confirm clipboard/file sync STILL works end to end. (C) known limitations: no Android SDK in CI sandbox so APK not built here; Android 10+ background clipboard-read restriction; relay must be reachable for off-LAN sync.
Add a short SECURITY note (in ARCHITECTURE or a SECURITY.md) stating payloads are end-to-end encrypted and the relay is zero-knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: README.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/VERIFICATION.md all exist and are internally consistent with the implemented modules.
VERIFICATION.md explicitly covers the off-LAN / 'phone far away' test via the deployed relay.
ROADMAP.md clearly marks Phase 1 scope vs. later phases.
Docs reference the actual module names and gradle commands used in this project.
verification: Confirm the four doc files exist and reference real modules (:core, :relay, :app) and real commands (`./gradlew :core:test :relay:test`).
Read VERIFICATION.md and confirm it contains both the same-Wi-Fi and the remote/mobile-data test paths.

(#4 short code) SECURITY.md and ARCHITECTURE.md no longer claim a working short-code-to-pending-pairing resolution; they state pairing is by QR scan or pasting the full payload and that short-code resolution is not wired in Phase 1. All docs reference the real modules (:core, :relay, :app), real class names (Envelope, WireJson, Framing, Pairing, PairingPayload, E2E, EnvelopeCodec, RelayHub, Routing/Hello, RelayClient, LanTransport, TransportRouter, SyncService, PairingManager, ClipboardSync, ScreenshotCapture, FileShare), and real commands (./gradlew :core:test :relay:test, ./gradlew projects, ./gradlew :relay:run).
